about: DAS's published measurements; the release summary's DAS entries are built from it
build: Andrey development build of 18 November 2026 (version string 0.17.1, the functional-models line with DAS as released in 0.18.0); the 0.19.0 release branch returns the same graph on 40 of 40 check datasets (50 variables, ER4, raw and z-scored)

comparators.dodiscover: DAS in dodiscover at commit 6e644561, the code published with the DAS paper, DAS(eta_G=0.001, eta_H=0.001, alpha=0.001, das_cutoff=0.01, min_parents=5, max_parents=20, n_splines=10, splines_degree=3), the paper's settings, with torch 2.13.0+cpu
comparators.cam: andrey.cam at its defaults, the same build
comparators.score_matching: andrey.score_matching at its defaults, the same build
comparators.nogam: andrey.nogam at its defaults, the same build, at 10 and 20 variables

verdict_rule: DAS: per cell (scale, graph density, variables; 20 datasets): D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, on the datasets both fitted; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0). The decision cells are the z-scored and rescaled ones (claim in); the raw cells, where the reference reads the simulation's units and Andrey standardizes inside its order search, are reported, not judged (claim out). A cell worse on its first seeds was rerun on fresh seeds (replication); no decision cell was worse, so none was rerun, and the raw ER1 cells at 20 and 50 variables, worse on their first seeds, were rerun. result is the published verdict, better or worse only where the fresh seeds agree and a tie otherwise; replicated says which. The floor, each row's floor field, per dataset: SHD(Andrey) minus SHD(empty graph), with the same bootstrap; it applies where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, and a row then passes when Andrey's does too. The lane file's floor section takes the better of the empty graph and the complete DAG in column order
seeds_note: DAS: every cell holds 20 datasets: seeds 0-19 for ER1 and for ER4 at 10 variables; seeds 20-39 for ER4 from 20 to 200 variables, kept apart from the ER4 seeds 0-19 used while the method was built; the raw ER4 cell at 50 variables is the one on seeds 0-19, reported as context, with the reference's fits from a separate run on the same datasets. A replication holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39. The lane file's rows at 500 and 1,000 variables use seeds 0-19, and its paired check at 500 seeds 0-4
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, one timed fit without warm-up; a cap of 1,800 s per fit up to 100 variables and 3,600 s at 200 and above (the frontier's rows at 500 and 1,000 included), and 7,200 s for the authors' code in paired_at_500; past the cap a fit is a timeout and never scored as a graph. Two fits timed out, both SCORE's at ER4 with 500 variables (the frontier); no other fit failed or timed out. Times are process CPU seconds

regimes.score_paper_standardized: the papers' simulation: Erdos-Renyi graphs with d edges (ER1) or 4 d (ER4), each link one draw of a Gaussian process over the node's parents, Gaussian noise of variance uniform on [0.4, 0.8], 1,000 rows, every column z-scored
regimes.score_paper_rescaled: the papers' simulation: Erdos-Renyi graphs with d edges (ER1) or 4 d (ER4), each link one draw of a Gaussian process over the node's parents, Gaussian noise of variance uniform on [0.4, 0.8], 1,000 rows, each variable divided by its standard deviation before its children read it
regimes.score_paper: the papers' simulation: Erdos-Renyi graphs with d edges (ER1) or 4 d (ER4), each link one draw of a Gaussian process over the node's parents, Gaussian noise of variance uniform on [0.4, 0.8], 1,000 rows, in the simulation's own units

floor.about: DAS's SHD minus the better of the empty graph and the complete DAG in column order, per cell; the truth scored per dataset; pass when the 95% interval lies below 0

order_floor.about: z-scored, up to 200 variables: the share of true edges SCORE's order (DAS's order) puts in the true direction minus R2-SortnRegress's; pass when the 95% interval lies above 0. Every edge of DAS's graph points forward in that order on every dataset

frontier.about: z-scored: each comparator's SHD minus DAS's (mean, 95% interval) and its time over DAS's (median of the per-dataset ratio, 95% interval); a comparator dominates DAS when both intervals lie below 0 and 1. A timeout is a timeout, never a graph. Rows with fewer than 20 datasets are descriptive

paired_at_500.about: the authors' code at 500 variables, ER4, z-scored, seeds 0-4, a cap of 7,200 s, one fit per single-core job on an AMD EPYC 9555; descriptive (5 datasets). Andrey's fits ran on an AMD EPYC 9534, so the time ratio crosses CPU models

paper_check.about: DAS's mean SHD against the paper's Tables 1-2 (mean and SD over its 10 runs, raw columns); Andrey's graph is the same on z-scored and raw columns. Causes of the cells above the paper's mean + 2 SD, ranked: (1) on ER1, the standardized order search, since the paper ran raw columns whose variance grows along the causal order: in scale_trace the unscaled order search lands inside the paper's limit at 20 variables (4.35 and 3.7 against 6.0) and at 50 (16.35 and 14.5 against 24.1), the shipped DAS outside it (8.15 and 7.2; 28.3 and 28.65); not measured at 500. (2) ER4 at 500 is not explained by (1), since on raw ER4 columns DAS made as few errors as the authors' code or fewer up to 50 variables; no raw-column reference fit exists at 500, and the paper's 10 runs against these 20 are a minor factor

scale_trace.about: raw ER1 cells, where DAS made more errors than the authors' code on the first and the fresh seeds: DAS refit with its order search on the centered columns, unscaled (a development variant, not an option of the method), minus the authors' code on the same datasets. The unscaled order search closes the gap: the code published with the paper reads the columns' scales, which grow along the causal order in this simulation (varsortability 0.8-0.9), and DAS reads standardized columns by design
